newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes up, China supports Indonesian grades.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes up, China supports Indonesian grades.

text.p: Asian crude prices were firmer on Friday, supported by the short-covering of futures after the slump in prices earlier this week.
Strong buying interest for light sweet grades bolstered MidEast wet crudes and China demand to replenish stocks ahead of Chinese New Year was supporting Indonesian grades.
January Brent futures ended 28 cents higher on SIMEX at $22.80 per barrel, from London's Thursday settlement of $22.52.
Last Friday, January settled at $23.74 but a rise in U.S. crude and product stocks in figures out this week plus news Iraq was clinching its first export deals turned sentiment lower.
The Brent weakness saw Brent/Dubai coming in slightly.
Only offers were seen for the bulk of the day for February Brent/Dubai at $1.80 versus late New York offers of $1.83. There was little talk of January ahead of futures expiry on Monday.
Three February Oman deals emerged -- all into China at prices ranging 22/23 cents over MPM, reflecting China demand. But prices were not as high as recent deals of plus 25 cents.
Traders said China was aggressively buying regional crudes and has been the main supporting factor for Indonesian grades.
Winter demand and rising refining capacity helped Qatar grades.
Traders said Qatar Marine has traded at premiums of 58 to 65 cents over QGPC in recent days, while Qatar Land has traded at 70 cents over, firmer than the tone in recent weeks.

Minas, which has traded as high as ICP plus 65 cents, was assessed as high as 65 on the bid and 80 on the offer. Widuri, which has traded as high as 74 cents, was now seeing bids at that level and offers stepping back to 80 cents.

Indonesian sellers had worried January arrivals of West African crude would displace their grades. But China appears to be replenishing crude and product stocks, and running refineries at higher levels in the run up to Chinese New Year in February.
